digest.headline: Paramount Threatens California Exit Amidst Global Media Industry Shifts
digest.lead: Paramount is considering relocating operations from California and New York due to escalating legal battles. Meanwhile, the United Kingdom media landscape faces regulatory scrutiny as Disney+ secures a major podcast partnership to challenge Netflix.

Virgin Media O2 has added the Tennis Channel to its streaming line-up at no extra cost.
Sky is bringing back Saturday Night Live UK for six more episodes with its full original cast.

Grampian Hospital Radio has received the King's Award for Voluntary Service to recognise decades of volunteer dedication.

Samsung TV Plus has added nine new dedicated channels in the UK through an expanded partnership with All3Media International.

paragraphs: Disney+ has agreed a one-year sponsorship and content deal with Gary Neville's sports platform, The Overlap. The streaming service will become the headline sponsor for Stick to Football and a new format called Stick to United. This move is seen as a direct response to Netflix's partnership with Goalhanger.

Warner Bros Discovery Access has commissioned UK production companies Project Must Entertainment, 7Fifty, and Double FTV. These producers will create culinary programming for the Food Network brand and the Discovery+ streaming platform.

Samsung TV Plus has expanded its partnership with distributor All3Media International. The deal adds nine new dedicated FAST channels to the platform's line-up in the UK, France, and Spain. Meanwhile, Virgin Media O2 has added the Tennis Channel to its streaming line-up for Virgin TV customers.

Media regulator Ofcom is investigating GB News following 12,000 complaints about a guest's remarks. The guest appeared to link pride parades with bestiality and paedophilia. The incident has set a potential record for complaints against the broadcaster.

Ofcom has also found Nation Radio London in breach of broadcasting rules. The station aired a prohibited political advertisement. The broadcast occurred despite the script receiving prior clearance from Radiocentre.

UK brands are adapting their media strategies to align with new regulations on HFSS in-store promotions. The restrictions on high fat, sugar, and salt products have doubled interest in omnichannel advertising. Brands are developing targeted campaigns to navigate the rules across different channels.

The UK fixed broadband market has entered a flat phase, according to data from Point Topic. Total retail and wholesale connections reached 29.37 million at the end of the second quarter of 2026. This represents an increase of just 1,000 connections quarter-on-quarter.

Journalist Ray Snoddy has highlighted issues with how The Times reported its own radio station's listener figures. The investigation suggests there was under-reporting of RAJAR data. This has raised questions about transparency in media reporting.

The Alliance of Media Research Analysts has expanded its annual awards by adding six new categories. These additions address the underrepresentation of regional and independent agencies. They also recognise the growing role of adtech in media research and honour the late judge Denise Turner.

Lyca Radio is set to expand its Midlands network by launching full DAB coverage in Birmingham. The transition will take place on 1 September. This move will allow the station to reach a wider audience in the region.

Grampian Hospital Radio has been honoured with the King's Award for Voluntary Service. The award recognises decades of dedication by the station's volunteers. The team has provided entertainment and comfort to patients for many years.

UK video-first podcast company Jampot has partnered with Sony to upgrade its production capabilities. Jampot has deployed a range of Sony cameras and solutions to support its growing slate of visual podcasts. This setup aims to deliver cinematic quality for digital listeners.

Paramount Skydance CEO David Ellison is facing an antitrust lawsuit over his proposed purchase of Warner Bros. Discovery [14]. Ellison has threatened to move Paramount out of California if the suit is not settled [3, 17]. The Writers Guild of America has criticised the threat, stating it justifies blocking the merger [32].

Paramount executives confirm that leaving California is under consideration [17, 18]. The company is also considering moving CBS News out of New York City as legal battles with state attorneys general intensify [16].
Before the lawsuit to block the Warner deal was filed, Paramount discussed creating an oversight committee [35]. This board would ensure the independence of CNN under the merged entity [35].

The Canadian Radio-television and Telecommunications Commission is considering a major policy shift [10, 11]. The regulator may remove licence expiry dates and issue indefinite television broadcast licences [10, 11]. This proposal would affect major media companies including Bell Media, Rogers, and Corus [10, 11].
The CRTC has also administratively renewed several broadcasting licences to August 2027 [34]. These one-year extensions apply to broadcasters such as Bell Media, Rogers, Blue Ant, and Corus [18].

In the United States, low-power television advocates have petitioned the Federal Communications Commission [19]. They are seeking permission for voluntary 5G broadcasts, noting there is no ATSC 3.0 mandate for LPTV [19]. Meanwhile, Newsmax is preparing a lawsuit against the FCC over a recent broadcast television ownership vote [26].

Tech giants are stepping up their artificial intelligence and hardware offerings. Apple is in talks to pay publishers to use their content to improve its Siri voice assistant [20]. Meanwhile, Spotify has announced it will label AI-generated artists and avoid promoting them on its platform [21].

Google has launched its new Pixel 11 smartphone lineup alongside the Pixel Tag, a finder tag using emerging Bluetooth technology [15, 34]. Amazon is offering gift card promotions for preorders of the new devices [36].
In the AI sector, Anthropic is in talks to acquire Israeli startup Decart for 6 billion dollars [37]. The transaction would mark the largest acquisition in Anthropic's history [37].
Canadian cinema chain Cineplex has reported record revenue for the second quarter of the year [22]. The company experienced a 9.3 per cent increase in theatre attendance [22].

This attendance surge led to significant jumps in box office and food services revenue [22]. The company achieved its highest second-quarter box office performance since 2019, driven by a strong film slate [23].
Netflix has renewed its licensing deal for Seinfeld for another five years [24]. Paramount has also extended its basic-cable rights for the comedy series for three more years [24].

Broadcasters are preparing their autumn schedules. Corus Entertainment's Home Network has unveiled its fall slate of Canadian originals and global acquisitions [38]. Additionally, Peacock's drama Dig is scheduled to debut on Showcase and StackTV in November [33].

Disney is expanding its children's programming with a new hybrid live-action and animated series [39]. The show, Megan and Cupcake Ready for Preschool, will debut on Disney Junior and stream on Disney+ [39].
Corus Entertainment has secured a major sports broadcasting deal in Alberta. The Calgary Flames have signed a five-year radio partnership with Corus's QR 770 AM [25].

In the United States, National Public Radio has promoted two executives to senior digital roles [29]. Bryan Moffett becomes Senior Vice President of Transformation, and Michael Seifollahi becomes Vice President of Audience Technology and Data [29].
